newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dlr weakens slightly amid forex turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dlr weakens slightly amid forex turmoil.

text.p: The Singapore dollar weakend slightly in moderate trading early on Monday as Southeast Asian currencies took a battering from speculators, dealers said.
At 0215 GMT, the Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4427 to the U.S. dollar compared with an opening level of around 1.4410. It had traded at a high of 1.4395 and a low of 1.4440.
However, traders said the Singapore dollar should be largely immune from the turmoil affecting other foreign exchange markets in the region.
"The MAS (Monetary Authority of Singapore) has over US$60 billion in the bank and you can't short the currency," one trader noted.

He said Singapore's economy was still fundamentally sound -- the government forecasts 1997 economic growth at between five and seven percent -- and that the banking system was also a lot better off than some other countries in the region.

The Indonesian rupiah and the Malaysian ringgit were sold heavily by speculators on Monday morning following the de facto devaluations of the Thai baht and Philippine peso in the last couple of weeks.
